definition: A metric that measures the similarity between two vectors by computing the cosine of the angle between them, commonly used to compare embeddings.
details: Cosine similarity ranges from -1 to 1 and is widely used in semantic search and recommendation systems because it captures directional similarity independent of vector magnitude.
story: Imagine a driving test that every new model has to pass before it is allowed on the road. In plain words: A metric that measures the similarity between two vectors by computing the cosine of the angle between them, commonly used to compare embeddings. Here is how it actually plays out: Cosine similarity ranges from -1 to 1 and is widely used in semantic search and recommendation systems because it captures directional similarity independent of vector magnitude. It is the exam that keeps everyone honest. That shared ruler is Cosine Similarity.
